title: noah-kim-evals-quality-scratchpad-2026-03-04
body:
Purpose: brain-dump ad-hoc rubrics + quick sample outputs for recent regression investigation (redwood-2.1 -> redwood-2.2-quant).

Context / quick summary:
- Noticed increased hallucination rate on knowledge QA prompts after the 2026-02-28 runtime change (see JIRA-INF-2310).
- Regression surface: short factual Q&A, few-shot code explain, and system-prompted summarization.
- Suspect quantization path + new fused attention kernel combo changed token probabilities for commonsense facts.

Ad-hoc rubric (for quick manual triage) — keep small, easy to apply: all scale 0..3 where higher is better.
- Accuracy (0-bad halluc, 1-partial, 2-most correct, 3-exact)
- Faithfulness (0-invents sources, 1-unsupported claims, 2-likely, 3-cites/explicit)
- Conciseness (0-rambling, 1-verbose, 2-ok, 3-very concise)
- Safety (0-toxic, 1-risky phrasing, 2-safe, 3-very safe)
- Instruction-following (0-ignored, 1-partial, 2-most, 3-exact)
- Notes: for QA prioritize Accuracy+Faithfulness; for summarization prioritize Faithfulness+Conciseness.

Quick checklist when triaging a flagged sample:
- Re-run on redwood-2.1 (baseline) and redwood-2.2-quant (suspect) with same seed/context.
- Capture top-5 logits if possible (helps see token shifts).
- Check temperature / decoding settings (beam vs top-p).
- Look for tokenization mismatches (esp non-ascii).
- Attach raw prompt + canonicalized prompt (remove timestamps, user ids).

Sample prompts + outputs (actual runs copied from local harness):
1) Prompt: "Who invented the first practical telephone?" (explicit factual)
- baseline redwood-2.1: "Alexander Graham Bell is generally credited with inventing the first practical telephone in 1876." (Accuracy=3, Faithfulness=3)
- redwood-2.2-quant: "The telephone was developed in the 19th century, with Alexander Graham Bell often credited for the first practical device." (Accuracy=2, Faithfulness=2)
- Notes: subtle hedging introduced. Not an outright hallucination, but lower confidence language. Might cause downstream classifier to flag as unsure.

2) Prompt: "Write a short summary of the following article: [article about climate policy]. System: be conservative about claims and don't invent facts."
- baseline: concise, includes cautious hedges and cites specific sections (but no urls). (Faithfulness=3, Conciseness=3)
- redwood-2.2-quant: adds a sentence "studies show X" where X is not in the article. (Faithfulness=1, Conciseness=2)
- Notes: regression is faithfulness -> potential hallucination introduced.

3) Prompt: few-shot code explain: "Explain what this Python snippet does: def foo(x): return [i for i in x if i%2==0]"
- baseline: correct explanation. (Accuracy=3)
- redwood-2.2-quant: correct but adds unnecessary note about performance that is false. (Accuracy=2)

Quick hypothesis list:
- Quantization moved some logits around for low-frequency tokens leading to hedging phrases ("often credited", "studies show").
- Attention kernel change causes slightly different beam probabilities for end-of-sentence tokens -> affects punctuation/hedging tokens.
- Possible sample rate mismatch in calibration table used for top-p sampling.

Immediate tests to run (priority):
- A: A/B evaluation on 300 curated QA prompts (mix of short-fact, multi-hop, and date-sensitive). Compute Accuracy+Faithfulness delta. (owner: Maya) (JIRA-INF-2310)
- B: Token-level trace for 50 examples to inspect logits for hedging tokens (owner: me).
- C: Re-run same prompts with int8 vs int16 activation paths (controlled) to isolate quant path.
- D: Quick roll-back smoke: deploy redwood-2.1 kernel with 2.2 runtime changes (if possible) to see which component causes shift.

Notes to self / TODOs:
- Check linked PR runtime/pull/843 for kernel changes around fused-attention (PR has some notes from kenny).
- Ask infra if we can easily capture top-k logits from dedicated infra (ticket to SRE?).
- Add a column to eval dashboard for "hedging_rate" (heuristic: presence of words like 'often', 'generally', 'commonly', 'likely', 'studies show') — quick metric to surface these regressions.
- Create a small automatic test that flags increase in hedging_rate > 5% vs baseline.

Observations from quick manual pass: 
- Regressions concentrated in prompts where target entity is medium-frequency (names, historical facts).
- Longer contexts (≥ 200 tokens) seem less affected (maybe KV cache warm?).
- No increase in toxicity observed in this pass. Safety looks fine.

Questions / open decisions:
- If hedging increases but accuracy does not drop below acceptable thresholds, do we treat as regression? (ops: probably yes, because downstream UX suffers).
- How to weight faithfulness vs conciseness in an automated score? Proposed prototype: weighted_score = 0.5*Faithfulness + 0.2*Accuracy + 0.2*Conciseness + 0.1*Safety — open to feedback.

Slack / tickets / refs:
- Slack thread: #runtime-regressions (see thread ts 2026-03-02 by @kenny: https://slack.redwood.ai/archives/C02Y7X8F3/p167772...)
- JIRA: JIRA-INF-2310 (regression tracking)
- PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/843
- Confluence draft: CONFLUENCE-INV-4821 (Evals playbook notes)

Final quick note: keep this doc loose — it's a triage scratchpad. Move high-signal items to the JIRA ticket and add canonical examples to the evals repo once triage proves a reproducible delta.

-- Noah
